sources.note: Not a Toka-Leya source: texts are Lenje (Bene-Mukuni) and Rhodesian Tonga; 'Toka'/'Leya' do not occur. Preliminary notes cover orthography only; the only accent remark is a footnote on an interjection ('Pronounce it baacwo! with the tonic accent on baa'), not a stress rule.

sources.citation: Siampwili, Royce S. 2020. The significance of selected forms of address in Toka-Leya: a socio-pragmatic perspective. MA (Linguistic Science) dissertation, University of Zambia. 124 pp. https://dspace.unza.zm/handle/123456789/8122

sources.citation: Sawka, Kenneth S., Christopher Mbewe, Daka Josephat & Jacob Schwertfeger. 2019. Toka-Leya of Zambia: Southern Province: Livingstone, Kazungula, Zimba, and Kalomo Districts. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2019-003. Dallas: SIL International. 74 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. sources.citation: Carter, Hazel. 2002. An outline of Chitonga grammar. Lusaka: Bookworld Publishers. (Plateau Tonga, M64, glottocode tong1318)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Toka-Leya is conventionally treated as a dialect of Tonga (Ethnologue; Siampwili 2020; SIL 2019 measured 62% lexical similarity and calls it distinct). A modern Tonga grammar is the nearest description with a prosody statement; it would apply to domb1246 only by extension and should be logged under tong1318, not as a Toka-Leya statement.
